subsystems.name: EMI filter and rectifier
subsystems.role: cleans incoming mains power and turns alternating current into rough direct current.

subsystems.name: Power-factor-correction stage
subsystems.role: draws current smoothly from the mains so the supply looks like a resistor to the grid.

subsystems.name: Primary switching stage
subsystems.role: chops the high-voltage DC at tens to hundreds of kilohertz.

subsystems.name: Secondary rectification and filtering
subsystems.role: converts the transformer's high-frequency AC back to the low DC rails the PC uses.
parts: synchronous rectifier MOSFETs or Schottky diodes

subsystems.name: Regulation and protection
subsystems.role: keeps 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V accurate and shuts the unit down on fault.

subsystems.name: Thermal and mechanical
subsystems.role: removes waste heat and delivers power to connectors.

buildSteps.title: Define the rails and topology
buildSteps.detail: Engineer picks total wattage, the split between 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V, and whether to use a double-forward or LLC resonant design.

buildSteps.title: Wind the transformer
buildSteps.detail: Ferrite core, copper windings and insulation are assembled to a turns ratio that steps hundreds of volts down to about 12 V, with creepage distances meeting safety rules.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the PCB
buildSteps.detail: Surface-mount resistors, capacitors and control ICs are reflow-soldered; large parts like the bulk capacitor, transformer and heatsinks are placed by hand or wave-soldered.

buildSteps.title: Mount and wire
buildSteps.detail: The board goes into the steel chassis, MOVs and fuses are fitted, the fan and cable harness are attached, and high-voltage joints are sleeved.

buildSteps.title: Burn in and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Every unit runs under load on a test rack; efficiency, ripple, hold-up time (mains-loss ride-through, typically 16 ms at full load) and protections are checked.

buildSteps.title: Certify
buildSteps.detail: Units are submitted for safety approval and for efficiency ratings, then labelled with the correct wattage and connector set.

prerequisites.why: the switching devices set how efficiently and how fast the supply can chop DC.
the transformer is the heart of the isolation and voltage step-down.
they smooth the rails and must survive years of heat.
they regulate output and manage protection without analogue tuning.
they allow smaller, cooler supplies, but cost keeps them out of most units.

pathway.unlocks: stable power for high-end graphics cards.

pathway.milestone: digital control with telemetry over a data link

pathway.unlocks: smaller, fanless or near-silent supplies at high efficiency.

pathway.milestone: higher-voltage DC distribution inside the case
pathway.unlocks: lower cable losses as component power keeps climbing.
